lessons: Do not re-implement designer animations as code. The hand-coded recipes in Motion Presets never matched Логошот, Titles or SMM: track mattes, nested precomps, blend modes and shape reveals were lost. Keep the designer-made comps as the source of truth and parametrise them (TXT_/BOX_/in-out contract, Essential Graphics). Build from code only for simple brand primitives and motion presets.

The vault claim 'MOGRT via ExtendScript is technically impossible' is wrong as stated. Premiere's sequence.importMGT(path, ticks, vTrackOffset, aTrackOffset) is proven in premiere-autopilot on 107 cards, with two caveats: about 4% were silently dropped (count and re-import), and the default length is 4.92 s (set end).
AE can author and export MOGRTs by script (Property.addToMotionGraphicsTemplate, CompItem.exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate, AE 15.1+).

What is verified impossible: setting the text of a Premiere-authored MOGRT. getMGTComponent() returns null and Source Text reads back as garbage, so the text must be baked into a per-card .mogrt with a fresh capsuleID (mogrtcard.py); otherwise Premiere's capsule cache can show the same text on several cards. Editing parameters of AE-authored MOGRTs through getMGTComponent().properties is untested here: test it first.

The vault's 'ExtendScript EOL in Sept 2026' is wrong. It came from Extensions-LLM-Chat_Pr/.omc/research/pp26-compatibility-analysis.md. Adobe's developer-blog post of September 2026 retires CEP, not ExtendScript ('ExtendScripts are not affected by this transition'). Premiere stops accepting new CEP submissions in Dec 2027 and disables CEP by default in Dec 2028; AE and AME disable CEP by default in Dec 2028; CEP is removed from the apps in Dec 2029. Premiere has GA UXP plus hybrid plugins; AE gets public-beta UXP plugins by Nov 2026. Locally, AE 26.3 ships a UXP folder holding only Adobe's Home plugin, while Premiere 26.3.2 bundles about 14 Adobe UXP plugins. Conclusion: CEP is viable now, but keep the core host-agnostic and the host adapters thin.

Cyrillic and other non-ASCII text: CEP's evalScript mangles it on Windows, so escape every argument to ASCII-only JSON (asciiSafeJson in Phygital host.js). Write the JSX source itself as ASCII and use no backslashes in it: use forward slashes plus new File(p).fsName. Copy binary files in Node, not with ExtendScript File.copy, which corrupted copies from Cyrillic paths. ae-motion-live quirk 77 also reports ExtendScript File() as flaky on non-ASCII paths, so keep the asset library under an ASCII root. On this PC even the extension folder and %APPDATA% sit under C:/Users/Глеб.
The package has 10 file names in Mac NFD normalisation (decomposed й). Normalise to NFC or ASCII slugs when building the library, or path matching fails on Windows.

Bridge reliability: CEP 12 cold starts return 'EvalScript error.', 'undefined' or '' at first. Retry only idempotent reads (0/300/900 ms) and never auto-retry a mutating call: the old retry re-applied edits 2-3 times. On a timeout the host keeps working, so poll a cheap read instead of re-issuing. Queue calls one at a time, because ExtendScript is single-threaded. Wrap every host function so it returns structured errors (_wrap). Guard JSON with a small polyfill, not json2.js, whose regex breaks the ES3 parse.

ES3 is strict and its failures are silent. ES5 features, reserved-word object keys and a negative number pasted after a minus (x--400000) all fail at parse time as an opaque 'EvalScript error'. In AE a syntax error raises a modal that blocks the bridge until a person dismisses it. Lint every payload (lint-jsx.js).

Other AE modals also block scripting: setting app.project.workingSpace, a non-zero displayStartTime during a render-queue render (suppression does not catch it), and saving during aerender. Never run AE calls concurrently.

Fonts: AE echoes back any font name you set, so the read-back proves nothing. Verify with app.fonts.getFontsByPostScriptName(ps)[0].location, where a phantom shows up as times.ttf. Use 'SBSansDisplay-Semibold' with a lower-case b. A missing glyph swaps the whole layer's font. Neither MOGRTs nor .aep files carry fonts, so the panel needs a per-machine font check.

Hint from the audit (heuristic): every '(converted)' project stores TimesNewRomanPSMT in its text documents where the originals store the SB Sans version string. The text may have been silently substituted at conversion; verify in AE before treating the converted files as the source.

Premiere time: work in ticks (254016000000 per second; per frame = 254016000000/fps). Converting seconds to ticks rounds down, and an off-grid overwriteClip rounds up. Assign whole Time objects: 'clip.start.seconds = x' is a silent no-op. Markers take seconds.
Premiere tracks: TrackItem.move() breaks track order. insertClip ripples only one track. seq.videoTracks.addTracks is undefined on 26.3.2; use QE addTracks after app.enableQE().

Premiere import and focus: importFiles is asynchronous and can return false with no exception or ignore the bin argument. Poll up to 8 s, retry once, and find the item by media path. app.project means whichever project is focused, and a click changes the active sequence. Act on the active sequence and refuse to act if there is none.

Dynamic Link is not a button-insert route. Guide-layer audio leaks into Premiere. Linked audio is conformed once and never refreshed (.cfa/.pek files next to the .aep). A second headless AfterFX (about 3.2 GB) starts, exports run about 7x slower, re-import duplicates items, and getOutPoint goes stale. Templates must be silent. For buttons in Premiere use MOGRTs or pre-rendered alpha clips.
AE keeps every imported footage file open (EBUSY on Windows). Write the new version under a new name, then call FootageItem.replace().

Rendering from Premiere: sequence.exportAsMediaDirect is synchronous, works only on the ACTIVE sequence, needs native paths and returns 'No Error' on success. The bridge may time out while the render continues: wait for the file and never re-issue.

Rendering from AE: queueInAME uses AME's LAST preset, and no API passes an .epr. AME's command line works only at launch, and its watch folders ignore comps inside folders. aerender with AE output-module templates (native H.264 OM, e.g. 'H.264 - Match Render Settings - 15 Mbps') plus ffmpeg is the predictable route. aerender renders the SAVED project; judge success with ffprobe, not the exit code.

Preset decode findings: Webinar presets are 24 fps against 25 fps comps, and SMM presets are 30 fps against 24/25 fps comps, so exports convert frame rates and judder. AME and Premiere list presets by <PresetName>, not by file name. SMM_1x1 uses level 5.2. The mode=3 and performance=1 values should be confirmed in the AME UI. Premiere 26.3.2 and AME 26.3.2 are installed. The user-preset folder is per AME major version (Documents/Adobe/Adobe Media Encoder/26.0/Presets) and currently holds one unrelated HEVC preset.

Presets for animations: none of the user's code uses AE layer.applyPreset with .ffx files, and Premiere has no known ExtendScript call to apply .prfpset effect presets. In Premiere, motion presets have to be MOGRTs or scripted keys on Motion/Opacity ComponentParams (addKey, setValueAtKey). Test both before promising them.

AE template mechanics: comp.duplicate() does not duplicate nested precomps. Set layer times in the order startTime, inPoint, outPoint. Turning timeRemapEnabled on resets outPoint. setValue on a property that has keyframes aborts the build mid-loop. AE will not import WEBP. Every template comp must be silent.
Undo and target: give each button press exactly one undo group (M.run). Never silently fall back to 'the first comp in the project' as Motion Presets does; refuse with a clear message instead.

Distribution: for dev, set PlayerDebugMode on both CSXS.11 and CSXS.12 (both are set on this PC). A signed ZXP (self-signed is enough) removes that need, but a signed install cannot self-update, because file hashes are verified; keep the brand library outside the extension folder and update it separately. Restart the host after installing, since CEP scans extensions only at launch. Use a real bundle id, not com.example.*. Give the panel its own .debug ports. Paths written from a Claude-managed shell can be MSIX-virtualised.

Versions: only AE 26.3 is usable on this PC; the AE 2025 folder is a remnant without AfterFX.exe. Templates saved in AE 26 open only in AE 26+, so set the manifest's minimum host version from the version the templates are saved in.

Brand canon conflicts must be settled before 'fixing' the projects: palette names (graphite #222222 vs #343F48), near-white #F7F7F7 (not a brand colour), the package's elastic logo overshoot against the motion stop-list, and fps per format (tokens say 25/30; the SMM comps use 24/25). All package projects use the legacy ExtendScript expression engine; consider switching to the JavaScript engine as part of the fix, after testing.

Read-only helper scripts left in the scratchpad: work/fontnames.py (PostScript names from font files), work/epr_dump.py and work/epr_table.py (.epr parameter-tree decoder). They are reusable in the library build and validation step.
recommended_stack:
Runtime: one CEP 12 bundle for both hosts.
- Use a real id such as ru.cloud.brandkit. List AEFT [26.0,99.9] and PPRO [26.0,99.9]; drop to 25.0 only if the templates are saved down to AE 25 and the MOGRTs are tested in Premiere 25.
- RequiredRuntime CSXS 11.0 as a floor (it loads on CEP 12). CEF flags --enable-nodejs and --mixed-context, so Node can copy files, read the library and presets, and scan fonts.
- Why CEP: it is the only third-party runtime both apps share today. Premiere has GA UXP; AE gets UXP only as a public beta from Nov 2026; CEP is disabled by default only in Dec 2028 and removed in Dec 2029.
- One shared client. Host adapters are loaded with $.evalFile according to csInterface.getHostEnvironment().appName: AEFT loads host/ae/*.jsx, PPRO loads host/ppro/*.jsx.
- Both adapters sit on a shared ES3 core: JSON guard, _wrap with structured errors, an {ok,…} result contract, and tokens.jsx.
- Keep the adapter interface small, about 10 calls: getContext, insertItem, setFields, applyMotionPreset, applyColor, importAsset, exportWithPreset, checkFonts, reveal, diag.

UI: Preact 10 + htm vendored as ES modules, with no bundler (proven in the Phygital Premiere panel).
- CSS is generated from the brand tokens JSON with the build-tokens.js pattern, which also emits tokens.jsx for both hosts.
- localStorage holds only UI conveniences.
- Bolt CEP (Vite + TypeScript, multi-host manifests, ZXP scripts) is an alternative if you want TypeScript and hot reload, at the cost of replacing tooling that already works.

Bridge: a single host.call() returning a Promise.
- Arguments are ASCII-only JSON (asciiSafeJson); calls go through a serial queue with a timeout per call.
- Cold-start retry for reads only. A mutating call is never retried: poll a cheap read instead.
- One undo group per click.
- Never act on an implicit 'first comp'.

Library: a versioned folder outside the extension, under an ASCII path, e.g. C:/CloudRu/BrandKit/vN or a shared drive.
- library.json lists each item with: id, title, category, type (mogrt, aep-template, alpha-mov, ffx, epr, svg or palette), hosts, formats (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3), fields, duration with in/out markers, and a thumbnail plus preview.
- A Node script builds and validates it from the fixed AE projects:
  - NFC/ASCII names;
  - fonts checked by PostScript name;
  - fps and size per format;
  - silent audio;
  - the TXT_/BOX_/in-out contract checked with G.tplProblems.
- The .epr presets ship inside the library and are passed by absolute path. Installing them into Documents/Adobe/Adobe Media Encoder/26.0/Presets is optional, so they also show up in AME and Premiere.

Premiere actions:
- Insert a MOGRT at the playhead with seq.importMGT on the first free track, snapped to ticks. Set its parameters through getMGTComponent (test first), or use pre-baked per-text MOGRTs from a mogrtcard-style generator.
- Insert alpha clips with importToBin + insertToTimeline (Phygital).
- Motion presets are MOGRTs or scripted Motion/Opacity keys.
- Export with the Cloud.ru presets in one of two ways:
  - sequence.exportAsMediaDirect(out, epr, app.encoder.ENCODE_IN_TO_OUT): synchronous and proven;
  - app.encoder.encodeSequence(seq, out, epr, workArea, removeOnCompletion, startImmediately) + app.encoder.startBatch() for the AME queue, with bind('onEncoderJobComplete'): Adobe's documented API, not yet used in the user's code, so test it first.

AE actions:
- Instantiate a template: import that element's own small .aep (ImportOptions with ImportAsType.PROJECT; test first), or build it from code with M.* and K.*. Then fill the TXT_ fields and fit the length by time remap (G.buildSlot).
- Apply .ffx animation presets with layer.applyPreset (test first).
- Apply colours to native targets, not through a Fill effect.
- Render through the render queue with output-module templates, or with aerender. queueInAME uses AME's last preset, so it cannot apply a specific .epr; AME's own ExtendScript DOM over BridgeTalk is another route to test.

Tooling:
- Node 22 or newer.
- node --test with lint-jsx.js and ae-mock.js for host code; a Premiere mock still has to be written.
- vitest or jsdom for the UI; build-tokens --check in CI.
- Live E2E through the existing CDP helpers on new .debug ports (e.g. 8094 AE, 8096 Premiere; 8088, 8092, 8098, 8099 and 8100 are taken).
- Packaging: ZXPSignCmd with a self-signed certificate builds the ZXP, installed per user with UPIA or ZXP Installer. No .debug file in a release. Library updates are decoupled from code updates.

UXP path: keep the business logic in pure modules with no CSInterface or ExtendScript in the core, so the Premiere adapter can move to UXP before Dec 2028 and the AE adapter once AE UXP leaves beta.
